label: Monthly revenue by subscription tier (last 12 months). SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline. TimescaleDB engine effect: chunk pruning on invoices hypertable (created_at >= NOW() - 12 months skips older 7-day chunks). Naive schema: 7-day chunk interval (TimescaleDB default).

Full invoice fetch via 4-table JOIN: invoices → users → invoice_lines → products. SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline. No chunk pruning — query by invoice id (not partition column). invoice_lines.invoice_id FK dropped for hypertable compatibility (JOIN works via index). Pool of 1,000 invoice IDs.

Active session + cart retrieval by user_id under 50 concurrent threads. One psycopg2 connection per thread (thread-local). sessions is a plain PostgreSQL table (not hypertable). SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline. Pool of 1,000 user IDs.

Top-10 co-purchase recommendations via 2-hop self-JOIN on order_items. SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline. order_items and orders are plain PostgreSQL tables (not hypertables). No chunk pruning — TimescaleDB engine effect expected to be zero. Pool of 500 product IDs with co-purchase history.

Full-text product search using tsvector GIN index + ts_rank_cd. SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline. products is a plain PostgreSQL table — no hypertable, no chunk pruning. TimescaleDB engine effect expected to be zero for this query. 25 domain-relevant search terms, random per iteration.

All events for a user in a 30-day window, ordered by occurred_at DESC. SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline. TimescaleDB engine effect: chunk pruning on events hypertable — 30-day window touches ≤5 of ~104 7-day chunks. Naive schema: 7-day chunks (default). Window centred ±15 days on sampled anchor event — guaranteed non-empty. Pool of 1000 (user_id, anchor) pairs.

7-day rolling average of daily revenue per tier over 183 days. SQL identical to PostgreSQL baseline: generate_series gap-fill + raw invoices scan + LATERAL temporal tier attribution + window function. TimescaleDB engine effect: chunk pruning on invoices hypertable — 6-month window touches ~26 of ~104 7-day chunks. Naive: no continuous aggregate (that is the optimised schema). Invoice range: 2024-01-01 → 2025-12-31.

Monthly revenue by tier (last 12 months). Subscription: time_bucket('1 month', day) on daily_revenue_by_tier continuous aggregate — no raw invoice scan. Marketplace: raw LATERAL temporal attribution (unavoidable). 1-month invoice chunks.
Full invoice fetch via 4-table JOIN. Identical to naive — no TimescaleDB benefit for point lookups. Pool of 1,000 invoice IDs.
Active session + cart retrieval under 50 concurrent threads. Identical to naive — sessions is a plain table. Pool of 1,000 user IDs.
Top-10 co-purchase recommendations via 2-hop JOIN. Identical to naive — order_items/orders are plain tables. Pool of 500 product IDs.
Full-text search via tsvector GIN index + ts_rank_cd. Identical to naive — products is a plain table. 25 search terms, random per iteration.

All events for a user in a 30-day window. SQL identical to naive. Schema effect: 1-month chunks (30-day window touches 1-2 chunks vs ≤5 with 7-day chunks) + compression segmentby=user_id (contiguous user segments). Pool of 1,000 anchor pairs.

7-day rolling revenue average per tier over 183 days. time_bucket_gapfill('1 day', day) on daily_revenue_by_tier continuous aggregate — native gap-fill, no raw invoice scan for subscription component. Marketplace via small raw LATERAL. Rolling average via window function. Aggregate range: 2024-01-03 → 2025-12-31.
